page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Split into two A.P.s of n terms each
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both A.P.s must be named with their own a and d, and each must be given n terms, not 2n.
steps.memory_tip: Alternate terms give two lists, 2, 5, 8 and 3, 6, 9, and both have common difference 3.
lines: The differences run 1, 2, 1, 2, …, so the 2n terms are not one A.P.
Take the terms in alternate positions:
1st, 3rd, 5th, … give  2, 5, 8, …  : an A.P. with a = 2, d = 3, n terms
2nd, 4th, 6th, … give  3, 6, 9, …  : an A.P. with a = 3, d = 3, n terms

recall.must_convey: That the 2n terms split into two A.P.s of n terms each: 2, 5, 8, … and 3, 6, 9, …, both with d = 3.
accept: the whole thing is not an a p so split it
odd places give two five eight and even places give three six nine
two arithmetic progressions of n terms each with common difference three
rendu a p lu ga split cheyyali, each n terms
take alternate terms to make two progressions

steps.why: Consecutive differences run 1, 2, 1, 2, …, so the whole list is not an A.P. Taking alternate terms gives two A.P.s that both have common difference 3.
common_mistakes: Treating the whole list as one A.P. with d = 1.
Giving each part 2n terms instead of n.

steps.label: Add the two sums
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Check with n = 2, which is 4 terms: 2 + 3 + 5 + 6 = 16, and 3(2²) + 2(2) = 16.
steps.memory_tip: Two A.P.s share the factor n/2: add the brackets, then halve 6n + 4.

recall.must_convey: That the two sums are n/2(3n + 1) and n/2(3n + 3), and together they give S = n(3n + 2).
accept: use the sum formula on each progression
add the two brackets three n plus one and three n plus three
the answer is three n squared plus two n
rendu sums add cheste n into three n plus two
n by two into six n plus four is n into three n plus two
heard_as: three n squared plus two n
n into three n plus two

steps.why: Both parts share the factor n/2, so the brackets can be added before multiplying, and the 2 inside 6n + 4 cancels with the half.
common_mistakes: Putting n = 2n into the sum formula, which counts every term twice.
Giving the answer in terms of 2n and doubling it a second time.
